newsitem.title: USA: Money managers shorten U.S. debt positions - survey.
newsitem.headline: Money managers shorten U.S. debt positions - survey.

text.p: U.S. money managers took shorter positions in U.S. debt markets over the past week, said a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"Money managers are short and getting shorter," the report said. "(They) are certainly not managing portfolios with any hint of 'irrational exuberance.'"
In the week ended January 14, duration bogey held steady at 4.20 on an arithmetic basis and dipped to 4.89 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index rose to 5.12 from 4.94 the prior week on an arithmetic basis. It fell to 5.15 from 5.46 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 7.16 percent from 6.45 percent.
Twelve percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 16 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active fell to 4.67 from 4.75 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
